title: Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria: The ADHD Emotional Pain Nobody Talks About
description: RSD causes intense emotional pain from perceived rejection. Common in ADHD, often mistaken for other conditions. What it is and how to manage it.

content.text: A friend takes too long to text back. Your boss gives mild feedback. Someone's tone seems off. For most people, these are minor annoyances. For people with RSD, they're devastating.

items: Intense emotional pain from real or perceived rejection

content.text: RSD isn't officially in the DSM, but it's extremely common in ADHD:
Up to 99% of adolescents and adults with ADHD report being more sensitive to rejection than their peers, with many experiencing intense emotional responses.
ADHD involves emotional dysregulation as a core feature—emotions are more intense and harder to manage. RSD is one manifestation.

items: Not trying things to avoid potential rejection
Not sharing opinions or being authentic
Social anxiety (but it's about rejection, not evaluation)
Bipolar disorder (but mood shifts are situational)
Borderline personality disorder (but overall functioning is different)
ADHD medications can help emotional regulation generally
Alpha-2 agonists (guanfacine, clonidine) may specifically help RSD
Some respond to rejection-reduction medications like MAOIs
Understanding that the feeling will pass (even if intense)
Waiting before responding (the feeling peaks and fades)

content.text: RSD is real, it's painful, and it's common in ADHD. Knowing what it is can help—you're not 'too sensitive,' your nervous system just responds intensely to social threat. Treatment for ADHD often helps, and understanding RSD can help you ride out the waves without making decisions you'll regret.
